questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Verb + Preposition: Agree WITH vs Agree TO
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"The administrative committee finally agreed ___ the employees' proposal for modern biometric access."
questions.explanation: Jab target koi formal proposal, plan, scheme ya terms ho, toh strictly preposition 'TO' ka use hota hai: 'agreed to the proposal'. 'Agree with' kisi vyakti ya unke personal opinion ke sath lagta hai ('agree with the judge').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Confusing Relational Pairs — Agree TO a proposal, but agree WITH a person.
questions.hint: Check karein ki target koi insaan hai ya formal prastav (proposal)?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Direct Transitive Verbs: Zero Preposition with 'Discuss'
questions.question:
Identify the option that correctly completes the sentence without grammatical pleonasm:
"The division bench met yesterday to ___."

options.text: discuss about the pending constitutional petitions
discuss on the pending constitutional petitions
discuss for the pending constitutional petitions

questions.explanation: 'Discuss' ek direct transitive verb hai jiska direct object bina kisi preposition ke aata hai ('discuss the petitions'). Iske sath 'about' ya 'on' lagana redundant pleonastic error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: The Direct Transitive Law — discuss (NO about), reach (NO to), order (NO for).
questions.hint: 'Discuss' ka matlab hi hota hai 'talk about something', isliye extra preposition ki zaroorat nahi hoti.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Comparative Preposition: Prefer X TO Y
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"The senior registrar clearly prefers electronic file tracking ___ manual paper registers."
questions.explanation: Verb 'prefer' aur adjective 'preferable' do entities ke comparative choice mein hamesha preposition 'TO' demand karte hain: 'prefer X to Y'. Inke sath 'than' lagana classic examination trap hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Comparative Preposition Law — Prefer X TO Y (Never Than!).
questions.hint: 'Prefer' ke baad comparative conjunction 'than' lagta hai ya preposition 'to'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:

options.text: Mr. Sharma is three years senior than me in the judicial service.
Mr. Sharma is three years senior to me in the judicial service.
Mr. Sharma is three years senior over me in the judicial service.
Mr. Sharma is three years more senior than me in the judicial service.

questions.explanation: Latin origin ke comparative adjectives jo '-or' par end hote hain (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) strictly preposition 'TO' lete hain, kabhi bhi 'than' nahi lete.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Comparative Preposition Law — Words ending in -or strictly take 'TO'.
questions.hint: Senior, junior, aur prior ke sath 'than' lagta hai ya 'to'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"The vigilance department accused the junior superintendent ___ accepting pecuniary benefits."
questions.explanation: Apradh ya dosh ka arop lagane ke liye 'accuse someone OF a crime' formula hota hai. 'Blame' ke sath 'for' lagta hai ('blamed him for negligence') aur 'charge' ke sath 'with' lagta hai ('charged with corruption').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Causal & Result Vectors — Accuse OF, but Blame FOR.
questions.hint: 'Accused' ke baad kaunsa preposition aata hai: 'for' ya 'of'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Select the correct form to fill in the blank:
"The Chief Justice and all bench members look forward to ___ the new cyber forensics facility."
questions.explanation: 'Look forward to' mein 'to' preposition of anticipation hai, infinitive particle nahi. Kisi bhi preposition ke baad verb hamesha GERUND (-ing form) mein aati hai: 'look forward to inaugurating'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Preposition + Gerund Law — look forward to + V-ING.
questions.hint: 'Look forward to' ke baad bare verb (V1) lagti hai ya -ing form (Gerund)?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Causal Vectors: Result IN vs Result FROM
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"The inadvertent omission of critical metadata resulted ___ the dismissal of the electronic petition."
questions.explanation: Sentence mein subject 'omission of critical metadata' Kaaran (Cause) hai aur object 'dismissal of the petition' Parinaam (Outcome) hai. Jab Cause subject hota hai aur aage outcome hota hai, toh formula 'Cause + resulted IN + Outcome' lagta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Causal & Result Vectors — Result IN (Produces Outcome) vs Result FROM (Arises from Cause).
questions.hint: Sentence mein pehle kaaran (cause) bataya gaya hai jo outcome ki taraf lead karta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Evaluative Adjectives: Good AT vs Good FOR
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"Our newly recruited network administrator is exceptionally good ___ configuring firewall security policies."
questions.explanation: Kisi technical skill, vishay ya talent mein nipun hone ke liye standard English collocation strictly 'GOOD AT' hai ('good at configuring'). 'Good in' bolna common bolchal ki galti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Evaluative & Emotional Adjectives — Good AT for skill/competence.
questions.hint: Skill ya subject mein kushal hone ke liye 'in' nahi, 'at' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct spelling and preposition:
"The Division Bench swiftly disposed ___ forty urgent civil misc appeals in the pre-lunch session."
questions.explanation: Petitions, files ya property ka formal nistaran karne ke liye legal English collocation strictly 'DISPOSE OF' (single 'f') hoti hai. 'Dispose off' (double 'f') completely galat spelling hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Statutory & Administrative Preposition Concord — Dispose OF (Single 'f' always!).
questions.hint: Dhyan dein: single 'f' wala 'of' sahi hota hai ya double 'f' wala 'off'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"The High Court's paperless court initiative provides a sustainable solution ___ chronic infrastructural shortages."
questions.explanation: Noun 'solution' kisi samasya ya challenge ke reference mein hamesha preposition 'TO' leta hai ('solution TO the problem'). Hindi mein 'samasya KA hal' bolte hain, isliye log '*solution of' chun lete hain jo wrong hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Noun + Preposition Syntactic Units — Solution TO, Key TO.
questions.hint: Samasya ke hal ke liye 'solution of' hota hai ya 'solution to'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Complete the official notification sentence with the correct pair:
"All subordinate judicial courts must abide ___ court rules and adhere ___ the roster timings."
questions.explanation: Compliance Triad ke established rules hain: 'abide BY' (court rules/orders) aur 'adhere TO' (timelines/roster). Doosra related word 'comply WITH' hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Statutory & Administrative Preposition Concord — abide BY, adhere TO, comply WITH.
questions.hint: 'Abide' ke sath 'by' aur 'adhere' ke sath 'to' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Direct Transitive Verbs: Physical Space Entry
questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"When the judicial magistrate / entered into the chamber, / the stenographer presented the file. / No error"
questions.explanation: Physical room, chamber ya building mein dakhil hone ke liye 'enter' direct object leta hai (entered the chamber). Yahan 'into' lagana redundant preposition error hai. 'Enter into' sirf abstract/contractual contexts mein valid hota hai ('entered into an agreement').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: The Direct Transitive Law — Physical room entry takes zero preposition.
questions.hint: Physical chamber mein enter hone ke liye 'into' lagta hai ya zero preposition?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12
